summary:
S.J. Res. 32 (118th Congress) is a joint resolution providing for congressional disapproval, pursuant to chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code (the Congressional Review Act), of a final rule issued by the Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection. The resolution states that Congress disapproves the rule entitled “Small Business Lending Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (Regulation B),” as published at 88 Federal Register 35150 (May 31, 2023), and declares that the rule shall have no force or effect.

The resolution invokes the procedures and legal consequences set forth in 5 U.S.C. §§ 801–808. If enacted, the resolution would nullify the rule, and under 5 U.S.C. § 801(b)(2) the rule would be treated as though it had never taken effect and the agency would be barred from reissuing the rule in substantially the same form without subsequent statutory authorization. The resolution contains no exceptions, conditions precedent, or delayed effective dates. It does not authorize or appropriate funds, and it does not amend the Equal Credit Opportunity Act or any other permanent statute beyond the effect produced through operation of the Congressional Review Act.

The measure passed the Senate on October 18, 2023, and as of the date reflected in the text, had not been presented to the President. The resolution’s sole function is to exercise the legislative veto mechanism available under the Congressional Review Act for this specific agency rule.
